flawed_step: Line 0012 (step 3 of the induction), together with the equality form of the lemma stated on lines 0003-0005: step 3 treats the dist[] values read during the (k+1)-th pass as the end-of-iteration-k values, so it concludes dist[u] EQUALS the minimum length over paths with at most k+1 edges. With in-place relaxation the values read inside a pass may already have been updated during that same pass, so relaxations cascade and dist[u] can be strictly SMALLER than that minimum. Only the inequality dist[u] <= min over paths with at most k edges is preserved.
counterexample: Graph: vertices s, a, u. Edges: s->a (weight 1), a->u (weight 1), s->u (weight 10). Run Bellman-Ford with the edge list in the order [(s,a), (a,u), (s,u)]. Initialization (k=0): dist[s]=0, dist[a]=dist[u]=infinity. Iteration 1 (k=1), relaxing in list order: (s,a) sets dist[a] = 0+1 = 1; (a,u) reads the just-updated dist[a]=1 and sets dist[u] = 1+1 = 2; (s,u) offers 0+10 = 10, no change. So after k=1 iteration, dist[u] = 2. But u does have a path from s with at most 1 edge (the direct edge s->u), so the lemma applies to u, and the smallest length of a path from s to u with at most 1 edge is 10 (the 2-edge path s->a->u is not admissible at k=1). The lemma asserts dist[u] = 10; in fact dist[u] = 2. Hence the lemma as stated (equality) is false, and step 3, which purports to establish exactly this equality at each iteration, is invalid. (The asker's own worry on line 0014 is precisely this phenomenon, and it does occur.) The repaired lemma -- dist[u] <= min length over paths with at most k edges, and dist[u] is always the length of some actual s-u walk -- is true and suffices for correctness, but it is not what is proved here.
reasoning_summary: The lemma is stated as an equality: after k iterations dist[u] equals the minimum length of an s-u path using at most k edges. Standard Bellman-Ford relaxes edges in place within a pass, so an edge relaxed later in the pass can read a dist value already improved earlier in the same pass, letting information travel more than one edge per iteration. I constructed a 3-vertex instance (s->a=1, a->u=1, s->u=10) with edge order (s,a),(a,u),(s,u) where after a single iteration dist[u]=2 while the true minimum over <=1-edge paths is 10, and u satisfies the lemma's hypothesis of having a <=1-edge path. This directly refutes the lemma and the step-3 argument that maintains the equality; only the <= direction is invariant.
